messages:
alex_support: Customer reporting intermittent 401/403 when calling Redwood API from a Next.js app deployed to Vercel Edge (Edge Runtime). It works fine from their Node backend but fails from browser/edge context. They upgraded to edge-sdk v0.12.0 last week. Repro steps pasted below.

ben_support: Can you paste the minimal repro and network logs? Is this CORS/preflight related or auth header stripping?

alex_support: Repro (simplified):
```js
// pages/api/proxy (Edge runtime)
export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }
export default async function handler(req) {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}` , 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hi' }),
  })
  return new Response(await res.text(), { status: res.status })
}
```
They also call the SDK from the browser directly: `new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: window.__REDWOOD_KEY })` and get 401 in the client after a redirect or preflight. Network shows OPTIONS 204 then POST with missing Authorization header.

maria_engineer: Two quick asks: 1) exact SDK versions in browser and server (0.12.0 vs 0.11.x?), 2) full fetch request/response headers (copy from DevTools).

alex_support: Server uses edge-sdk@0.12.0 (same package used in both places). Browser bundle is a webpack/next compile that includes the edge SDK. Full headers snippet:
OPTIONS /v1/generate 204 (no auth header sent)
Request headers: Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method, Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type
Response headers: access-control-allow-origin: https://app.customer.com, access-control-allow-headers: content-type

Then client does POST but Authorization is missing when it reaches our ingress (auth header not present).

jess_ops: Could be service worker or a polyfill rewriting fetch/Headers. Vercel Edge runtime has native fetch but some bundlers polyfill (what bundler/plugins?) Also check if credentials/mode are set. If the browser does preflight and server's Access-Control-Allow-Headers doesn't include "authorization" (case-insensitive) the browser will drop it. Your response shows allow-headers only contains content-type — that would explain it.

marc_devex: Two notes: 1) older SDKs added a fetch wrapper that relied on a polyfilled Headers poly, which can cause header ordering/serialization differences. 2) In some user bundles we've seen `authorization` dropped due to a redirect (307/redirect to auth endpoint) where credentials are not forwarded. Does your ingress do any immediate redirect?

ben_support: Confirmed: ingress returns a 307 for token rotation path in some cases — that can strip Authorization unless fetch is configured with `redirect: 'manual'` or the server preserves auth on 307. Can you reproduce with a plain fetch from the page (no SDK) and compare?

alex_support: Reproduced with plain fetch — same missing header after preflight. Their CORS preflight response actually lacked the Authorization header in Access-Control-Allow-Headers. I asked them to change the server to echo `access-control-allow-headers: authorization, content-type` and it fixed the immediate repro.

maria_engineer: Good find. Still want to rule out SDK bundling issue. Please try pinning edge-sdk@0.11.4 in the frontend bundle (no server change) and repro — if header passes then it implies our bundle transform caused a change in how the header is emitted (rare but possible).

alex_support: Did a quick test — pinning to 0.11.4 didn't change the preflight behavior (still missing until server-side allowed headers fixed). So primary issue is CORS config on their ingress. However, we've also seen SDK upgrades change default fetch options used in edge runtime; worth auditing.

jess_ops: Action items: 1) Tell customer to include `authorization` in Access-Control-Allow-Headers on preflight and avoid redirects on token path, 2) We should add a note in the Edge SDK docs about bundlers/polyfills and CORS gotchas, 3) Dev to double-check edge-sdk behavior around redirect/fetch options.

marc_devex: I'll add a short doc snippet: recommend `fetch('/api/proxy', { credentials: 'include', headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer x' } })` when using cookies/credentials. Also call out that some service-worker setups can intercept and mutate headers.

ben_support: Customer followed our advice and updated CORS to include `authorization` and removed the immediate 307 redirect — their browser calls now succeed. They want us to track a better error message when the preflight disallows headers (currently just a 401 which is confusing).

maria_engineer: Agreed — we'll add clearer client-side detection and a log hint for missing Access-Control-Allow-Headers so support can triage faster. I'll file an internal ticket and follow up here.

deploy-bot: deploy:edge-sdk@0.12.1 scheduled to staging at 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z (cherry-pick: docs + client-side CORS hint) :rocket:

alex_support: Thanks — can we also get a short KB entry to send to customers explaining "why Authorization disappears in browser calls" with quick fixes?

marc_devex: Yep, I'll draft a KB and share a tiny snippet customers can paste into their CORS config and a minimal repro repo.

alex_support: Awesome, closing from our side — will reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
